title: A Material That Disappears Only Somewhere
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
The word biodegradable can create an impression that a discarded object will quickly disappear wherever it lands. In reality, decomposition depends on both the material and the environment. Temperature, moisture and the organisms present can determine whether a product breaks down within weeks or remains recognisable for a much longer period.

In a materials science seminar, students compared two packaging films. One was designed for industrial composting, where heat and moisture are carefully controlled. The other was intended to decompose under less demanding conditions. Rather than testing only in the environment recommended by each manufacturer, the students placed samples in three settings: a controlled composting unit, an ordinary garden compost pile and a container of cool water.

The industrially compostable film broke down rapidly in the controlled unit but changed little in the cool water during the observation period. The second film lost strength in the garden pile, although small fragments remained after the larger sheet had disappeared. The lecturer reminded students that fragmentation and complete decomposition are not the same thing. An object becoming difficult to see does not establish what has happened to its component substances.

The class then considered disposal instructions. A clearly labelled product could still cause problems in a town without a collection route to the appropriate treatment facility. Residents might place it in ordinary recycling, where it could interfere with the processing of other plastics.

The seminar's conclusion was that material design and waste infrastructure must be evaluated together. A promising laboratory result is not a complete description of environmental performance. To judge a packaging claim, we need to know the required conditions, the time scale and the likely destination of the product after use. The label alone cannot answer those questions.

questions.prompt: What mistaken impression can the word biodegradable create?
options: The object will break down quickly in any environment.
The material can never be used for packaging.
The product must be collected every day.
questions.answer: The object will break down quickly in any environment.
questions.explanation: 该词可能让人误以为物品无论丢在哪里都会迅速消失。

questions.prompt: What did the industrially compostable film do in cool water?
options: It broke down faster than in the controlled unit.
It made the water hot enough for composting.
It showed little change during the observation period.
It immediately became suitable for ordinary recycling.
questions.answer: It showed little change during the observation period.
questions.explanation: 适用于工业堆肥的薄膜在冷水中观察期内几乎没有变化。

questions.prompt: Why did the lecturer distinguish fragmentation from complete decomposition?
options: Small pieces becoming invisible does not show what happened to their substances.
Fragments can never move outside a compost pile.
All fragments necessarily contain more material than the original sheet.
Complete decomposition always happens before a sheet loses strength.
questions.answer: Small pieces becoming invisible does not show what happened to their substances.
questions.explanation: 大块变成难以看见的小碎片，不足以证明组成物质已经彻底分解。

questions.prompt: What must be considered alongside the design of a packaging material?
options: Whether its colour matches other products.
The number of students in the laboratory.
The size of the manufacturer’s advertising budget.
The available waste collection and treatment system.
questions.answer: The available waste collection and treatment system.
questions.explanation: 结尾强调材料性能要与当地收集和处理基础设施共同评估。
